B. Not to Improve This Highway Facility
The highway improvement is situated in an area that is becoming increasingly urbanized. When travelling through this area, it can be seen that new apartment houses and shopping complexes are being built. These new facilities, in addition to the past population increase, has and will generate an increase in the amount of traffic upon the traffic arteries.
The highway shoulders and roadway are in a state of deterioration. This condition is causing continuous maintenance costs and upkeep as well as potential safety hazards.
In brief, leaving the existing roadway without improvement would lead to increasing congestion and a reduced level of service as traffic volumes increase. With this would be the associated increase in accident rates, noise, air pollution, operating costs and impairment of access to abutting land and communities. This, in the long run, would lead to a reduction in the quality of the environment and would not comply with the goals and objectives of the transportation and local plans.
The projected average daily traffic for the "Do-Nothing" alternative would be 31,650 vehicles per day at an operating speed of 35 m.p.h. with 10 percent trucks. Based upon the "Manual for Highway Noise Predictions (short version)", Report No. DOT-TSC-FHWA-72-2, Chapter 3, the predicted traffic generated design year L10 noise level would be as follows:
.... 50 ft. from nearest traffic lane - 85dBA ....100 ft. from nearest traffic lane - 83dBA ....150 ft. from nearest traffic lane - 81dBA
The predicted average daily design year traffic for the "To Improve" alternative would be 31,650 vehicles per day at an operating speed of 40 m.p.h. with 10 percent trucks. The predicted traffic generated design year L10 noise level would be as follows:
.... 50 ft. from nearest traffic lane - 84dBA .... 100 ft. from nearest traffic lane - 81dBA .... 150 ft. from nearest traffic lane - 79dBA
